metadata.title: Thematic Analysis of Indonesian Physics Education Research Literature Using Machine Learning

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study does not use ILSA microdata (no student sampling frame, no assessment administration, and no questionnaire-based student records). Instead, it constructs a text corpus from 852 open-access conference proceeding PDFs and applies unsupervised topic modeling (LDA) to extract latent themes. Because there is no complex survey sampling or population-representative estimation, student/sampling weights and replicate weights are not applicable. The only data preparation steps reported are text scraping, cleaning (removing sections, names, references, stopwords), tokenization, lemmatization, and bigram construction before training the LDA model.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because the dependent variables are not cognitive achievement scores from an ILSA assessment; the study models latent topics from conference-paper text. Missing-data handling is not reported because the analysis is based on a curated set of documents (PDFs) and standard text preprocessing; there is no item-level missingness mechanism analogous to student response data in ILSA. Therefore, the usual PV and missing-data procedures for survey-based assessments do not apply to this dataset construction and topic-modeling workflow.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Collected open-access PDFs by manually downloading documents from five Indonesian PER international conference proceedings (2014–2021): ICRIEMS (n=152), ISSE (n=220), ICMSE (n=125), ICMScE (n=291), and ICoMSE (n=64), totaling 852 proceeding papers (~4–8 pages each). For each PDF, extracted text using pdfminer, then removed section headers (e.g., Abstract, Keywords, Figure, Introduction, Table, Method, Conclusion), authors’ names, affiliations, references, and acknowledgments; deleted numbers, symbols, punctuation, and English stopwords using nltk; tokenized into a document–word matrix; then used gensim for lemmatization and bigram detection (underscore-joined tokens). Further filtered the vocabulary by excluding words with frequency >55% and words with frequency <8 occurrences, reducing the vocabulary from 10,109 to 2,385 unique words/bigrams for LDA training.

main_findings.dataset_used: Indonesian PER conference proceedings (2014–2021; ICRIEMS, ISSE, ICMSE, ICMScE, ICoMSE)
main_findings.target_variable: Indonesian PER topic structure (8 latent topics)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Coherence values between 0.31–0.42; selected K=8 using elbow plot; face validity confirmed by PER experts (no predictive accuracy reported).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using Indonesian PER conference proceedings (2014–2021; ICRIEMS, ISSE, ICMSE, ICMScE, ICoMSE) the study leveraged unsupervised Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modeling to extract eight latent topic themes from the text corpus, finding that the dominant themes were educational technology, assessment, problem solving, and related PER areas. This indicates that automating literature synthesis with topic modeling can help the Indonesian PER community map research priorities and identify underexplored directions without manual keyword-only reviews.

main_findings.dataset_used: Indonesian PER conference proceedings (2014–2021; ICRIEMS, ISSE, ICMSE, ICMScE, ICoMSE)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Topic prevalence computed as within-year document mixture proportions; cumulative and 3-year rolling-window average prevalence visualized (Figures 7–8); jackknife resampling used to estimate standard deviation bands (up to 100 resampled values per year).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using Indonesian PER conference proceedings (2014–2021; ICRIEMS, ISSE, ICMSE, ICMScE, ICoMSE) the study leveraged LDA-derived topic mixtures to measure topic prevalence and track how each theme rose and fell across years, finding relatively similar rise/fall patterns with spikes around 2018–2019 and a later shift toward educational technology and problem solving. This indicates that PER research agendas in Indonesia evolve in response to curriculum and digital-technology demands, suggesting that funding and program planning should periodically rebalance support toward less prevalent themes such as physics laboratory work.

data.outcome_summary: This paper is a data-driven thematic analysis of Indonesian physics education research (PER) literature using unsupervised NLP. The authors manually collected 852 open-access conference proceeding papers from five Indonesian PER international conferences (ICRIEMS, ISSE, ICMSE, ICMScE, ICoMSE) published between 2014 and 2021, then scraped and cleaned the PDFs (removing headers, names, affiliations, references, acknowledgments; removing punctuation/numbers/stopwords; lemmatizing and detecting bigrams). They trained Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) models over a grid of topic numbers (K=4–14), alpha values (1, 5, 7.5, 10, 12.5), and random seeds, selecting K=8 based on coherence (0.31–0.42) and an elbow plot, with expert face validity. They then quantified topic development using topic prevalence (within-year mixture proportions) and visualized cumulative and rolling-window trends with jackknife-based variability bands. Because this is topic modeling on text (not ILSA achievement PVs), there are no PVs, survey weights, or student-level missing-data procedures; results are interpretive and depend on preprocessing and expert validation.
